To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of publication and citation indicators as tools in the management of university research is feasible; 2) the indicators are not perfect, but can be made reliable and valid by careful handling; 3) the indicators can be used for the monitoring of the performance of research groups, but not for the evaluation of individual scientists, because they are not sensitive enough to individual performance.
bibliometric indicators are a useful tool to monitor the performance of research groups and to identify the research groups which need special attention from the policy maker".

bibliometric data are not a substitute for the judgement of researchers and research managers, but that they can be used to stimulate a fruitful discussion between researchers and research managers on the performance of research groups and on the factors that influence research performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of bibliometrics as a research management tool, rather than as a research evaluation instrument.
the development of a "dialogue" between research policy makers and researchers.
the development of a methodology to make bibliometric data useful to university research management and policy making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bibliometrics is not yet ready for prime time, but is on its way.
, although the use of bibliometrics in research evaluation is problematic, it is also promising.
bibliometric data should not be used as an evaluation instrument, but that it should be used for monitoring purposes, as a tool in the dialogue with researchers and research policy makers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bibliometric indicators can be used as a "monitoring instrument" in university research policy.

the use of publication and citation data in research management can be a useful tool, if it is applied in a critical way and with the awareness that bibliometric results are not a substitute for other forms of evaluation, but a supplement.
bibliometric indicators can be useful for university research management when used in a proper way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use and interpretation of bibliometric data should be done in a collaborative and interactive way, involving researchers from all relevant disciplines.
bibliometric indicators can be used as a tool for the evaluation of university research.
the bibliometric approach to the assessment of research performance is not an alternative to peer review, but that the two approaches are complementary.
